# Script overview: 
This script responds to a reviewer request for additional population analysis.

# Inputs:
- "outputs/fullpaperdata.csv" (created in script 04)
- "outputs/tbl_s2.rds" (created in script 01)
- "processed_data/prisons_ca_flat.rds" (created in script 01)

# Key Outputs:
- "outputs/si_table_s3.csv" (Table S3)

```{r}
# Install pacman if not present
if (!requireNamespace("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pacman")

# Check, install missing, and load all packages in one call
pacman::p_load(tidyverse)

```


```{r}
# load main paper data
df1 <- read_csv("outputs/fullpaperdata.csv")
table(df1$carceral_sys)

# load df matching facilities to PWSIDs
tbl_s2 <- readRDS("outputs/tbl_s2.rds")
nrow(tbl_s2) # 345 (some have closed)

# load hifld data with population and facilities
prisons_ca_flat <- readRDS("processed_data/prisons_ca_flat.rds")
nrow(prisons_ca_flat) # 357

# make NAs explicit & simplify
prisons_ca_flat_pop <- prisons_ca_flat %>% 
  mutate(population = ifelse(population == -999, NA, population)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(facilityid, population)

# simplify
facility_pws <- tbl_s1 %>% 
  dplyr::select(facility_name, facilityid, pwsid, pws_name)

# join popn data to facility-pws data
facilities_w_pws <- facility_pws %>% 
  left_join(prisons_ca_flat_pop, by = "facilityid")
  
# sum popn by pwsid
facility_popn <- facilities_w_pws %>% 
  group_by(pwsid) %>% 
  summarize(sum_pop = sum(population))
  # note - if we want to remove NAs we can add na.rm=TRUE
  # but then PWSs that serve multiple facilities could look like they have a low
  # % of the PWS popn that is incarcerated, when that's really probably driven
  # by missing data for a key facility (eg. CDCR CALIFORNIA HEALTH CARE FACILITY
  # is missing data so it looks like it's only 3% carceral-serving, but that's likely
  # due to the fact that the main facility (i.e. CA health care facility) is 
  # missing data, while a smaller facility we identified as also served by the 
  # PWS has some data)
  #summarize(sum_pop = sum(population, na.rm=TRUE))
  
# join to main df
df <- df1 %>% 
  left_join(facility_popn, by = "pwsid")

# calculate percentage of the PWS popn that is incarcerated
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(pop_less_prison = population_served_count - sum_pop,
         pct_pws_pop_incarcerated = sum_pop / population_served_count * 100) %>% 
  mutate(pct_pws_pop_incarcerated = round(pct_pws_pop_incarcerated, 
                                          digits = 2)) %>% 
  relocate(sum_pop, pop_less_prison, pct_pws_pop_incarcerated, 
           .after = population_served_count) 

# categorize pws's based on % of PWS popn that is incarcerated
si_table <- df %>% 
  filter(carceral_sys != "other_water_systems") %>% 
  group_by(carceral_sys) %>% 
  summarize(n_pws_missing = sum(is.na(sum_pop)),
            n_pws_greater_half_carceral_pop = 
              sum(pct_pws_pop_incarcerated >= 50, na.rm=TRUE),
            n_pws_less_half_carceral_pop = 
              sum(pct_pws_pop_incarcerated < 50, na.rm=TRUE))

# create simpler version for manual review
pop_data <- df %>% 
  filter(!is.na(pct_pws_pop_incarcerated)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(pwsid, pws_name, pws_type_code, 
                population_served_count:pct_pws_pop_incarcerated,
                carceral_sys) %>% 
  arrange(pct_pws_pop_incarcerated)

# create Table S3 (focused only on partially carceral serving systems)
si_table_s3 <- pop_data %>% 
  filter(carceral_sys == "carceral_serving_water_system") %>% 
  dplyr::select(pwsid, pws_name, pct_pws_pop_incarcerated)

# save files
write_csv(si_table_s3, "outputs/si_table_s3.csv")

```
